chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Do not make the worship abhorrent to yourselves.

key_terms.الْعِبَادَةَ: worship (ritual acts like prayer, fasting, etc.)

ai.seo_question: How can one avoid burnout in religious practice according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of al-Kulayni’s chapter on moderation, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) warns against 'rigorism' (ghuluww) that leads to spiritual burnout, emphasizing that sustainable devotion is preferred over exhausting intensity. This principle aligns with the Shia scholarly understanding that worship should be consistent and beloved to the soul, preventing the self from developing aversion to religious duties.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from al Fazl Bin Shazaan altogether, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Do not make the worship to be abhorrent to yourselves’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma’il from Fadl ibn Shadhan all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
Do not cause your souls to dislike worship.’”
